_about: The check of the 59 option impacts on review-leftovers.html, 2026-09-20: two agent reviewers (is each consequence true · is the cost honest and the size right) and one agent verifier. Never hand-edited. Every CONFIRMED or PARTLY finding was applied; the refuted one is kept with the verifier's reason.

confirmed.claim: "I replace the old words in all 157 drawn strings of the lab's two files, and in the probe asserts that quote them. After it the lab says endpoint and login check everywhere, as the evaluation page does."
confirmed.problem: The 157 (11 norm lines + 146 strings, both counts check out) are only the strings the lab OWNS. The lab also draws three door sentences it does not own: the legend definitions it lifts from the suite station — `endpoint`, `middleware` and `role:gate` in _station.js, which is GENERATED from templates/center/shell/gabe-universe.html and must never be hand-edited. One of them, "the API door the frontend knocks on", is pinned verbatim by the probe as proof the lab reuses the legend's own words. So after the sweep the lab still says door on every head-strip chip and every function-role card, and removing those three means editing the suite station in both its copies (the two-file law) and regenerating _station.js — a suite change with its own battery and twins, not a words change.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/_station.js:1 ("GENERATED by gen-station-tokens.py from templates/center/shell/gabe-universe.html — never edit"), :147, :153, :172; gen-station-tokens.py:77 (LRDEF lift); endpoint-lab.html:291 (`Object.assign({}, S.LRDEF, …)`); _lab-ep-panels.js:2352, :2420, :2432 (`S.LRDEF["role:"+r]`); probe-eplab.mjs:263 (`/the API door the frontend knocks on/`) and :265 ("the legend's definitions are LIFTED, not retyped")
confirmed.fix: sweep: "I replace the old words in the {doorTotal} drawn strings the lab owns, the {oldWords} lines above included, and in the probe asserts that quote them. The lab still says door where it lifts the station legend's own sentences word for word: the endpoint kind's line, 'the API door the frontend knocks on', which the probe pins as verbatim, and the gate role's line. Changing those is a separate change to the suite station, in both its copies, with its own battery and the twins." Size stays words for the lab-owned part. The card's why needs the same caveat, because a sweep alone does not get to one word.
confirmed.why: The core claim holds. _station.js:1 is GENERATED from templates/center/shell/gabe-universe.html (gen-station-tokens.py:77 lifts `_LRDEF`). endpoint-lab.html:291 builds PLAIN from S.LRDEF and overrides neither `endpoint` nor `role:gate`. probe-eplab.mjs:263 pins "the API door the frontend knocks on" as verbatim, and :265 pins the lift itself. The door counter in gen-review.js scans only _lab-ep-panels.js and endpoint-lab.html, so these strings sit outside the 157. "Everywhere" is therefore false, and the card's why ("only a sweep gets to one word") fails with it. `_LRDEF` is the operator's own canonical legend column, so this could change his choice between sweep and keep, hence importance 3. Two details are overstated: only two lifted door sentences are drawn, `endpoint` (plainKey at endpoint-lab.html:386 and :391) and `role:gate` (_lab-ep-panels.js:2352, :2420, :2432, :2441, :2552, endpoint-lab.html:1702). The `middleware` line (_station.js:153) is lifted but no lab card draws it, and the endpoint line is on the kind chips, not on every head-strip chip.

confirmed.claim: "The line stays as it is. It keeps showing on the hover of that stage, in that topic."
confirmed.problem: Only the six `data` lines are drawn anywhere. STAGE_EXPECT declares six topics (data · schemas · functions · tests · widening · security = 36 lines), but every reader in the lab is `STAGE_EXPECT.data`: the DATA stage-header hover, the "also at" card, and the empty-stage placeholder. The other five parts have no stage surface at all — their registered variants are Shapes · Levels · Status · Ladder · Band, none grouped by stage. So 30 of the 36 lines the operator is asked to rule on show on no hover, in no topic; ruling "ok" keeps a sentence the lab never draws. The page nowhere says this.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/_lab-ep-panels.js:1237 (STAGE_EXPECT, six topics) vs its only three readers :1314, :1319, :1373 — all `STAGE_EXPECT.data`; part variants at :3594, :3606, :3614, :3620, :3624, :3628 (only `data` has "stages"/"stageblocks" at :3599-3600); docs/design/workflow-panel/endpoint-stages.md:58 states the intended `STAGE_EXPECT[topic][stage]`; probe-eplab.mjs:3300 reads `.data` only; review.words.json `norm_impacts.ok`
confirmed.fix: ok: "The line stays as it is. Only the Data topic's lines are drawn today: on the stage header's hover, on the 'also at' card, and as the text of a stage with no table. The lines of the other topics are written but drawn nowhere yet, so ruling them settles the words before their surface exists." Size stays none.
confirmed.why: _lab-ep-panels.js:1237 declares six topics, but the only readers are :1314, :1319 and :1373, all `STAGE_EXPECT.data`. PANELS (:3585-3630) gives a stage view to the Data part alone (`stages`, `stageblocks`); the other five parts register Shapes, Levels, Status, Ladder and Band. probe-eplab.mjs:3300 reads `.data` only. So the ok sentence is false for every line outside Data. Note that gen-review.js passes `norm_impacts` straight through (`normImpacts: W.norm_impacts`, no fill()), so this sentence cannot carry a token and must have no typed count. He still rules on the words either way, hence importance 2, not 3.

confirmed.claim: "I remove the line. That stage then shows no expectation for that topic, and says so, never a blank."
confirmed.problem: Nothing in the lab says so today. A missing key renders through `esc(undefined)`, which returns the empty string — the DATA topic's empty-stage div (`.sbnone`) draws literally nothing, and the stage-header card simply loses its plain line. Making it "say so" is a code change that does not exist yet, not a change to sentences. The strike also turns the probe red in three places: two asserts pin every topic's key list to exactly EDGE,GATE,INPUT,HANDLER,EFFECTS,ANSWER, and a third looks the data line up verbatim on the hover.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/_lab-ep-panels.js:1373 (`esc((STAGE_EXPECT.data||{})[s.key])`) with esc at :21 (`s == null ? ""`); :1314 plain line; probe-eplab.mjs:3016 (`ks !== 'EDGE,GATE,INPUT,HANDLER,EFFECTS,ANSWER'` for every topic) · :3308 (same for data) · :3304 (`h.indexOf(EXPECT[st]) >= 0`)
confirmed.fix: strike: "I remove the line. Where the lab draws it, which today is the Data topic only, a missing line would show as an empty space, so I add a fallback that says the stage has no expectation for that topic. The probe asserts that pin a line for every stage of every topic are rewritten with it." Size: lab.
confirmed.why: esc() at _lab-ep-panels.js:21 returns "" for a missing value, so :1373 would append an empty `.sbnone` div. At :1314 `plain` would be undefined, and hcard drops the plain line silently. Nothing says "no expectation" today, so that needs lab code. Probe asserts: the per-topic key check at :3016 feeds `ok(E6.bad.length === 0)` at :3019, and :3308 pins the six Data keys. The verbatim hover check at :3304 also fails when the struck line is Data EDGE, GATE, HANDLER or EFFECTS (`indexOf(undefined)` is -1). That is one to three asserts depending on the line, so the sentence should not carry a count. Lab code plus a probe rewrite is `lab`, not `words`.

confirmed.claim: "Every route's record stays 8 rows longer on this endpoint."
confirmed.problem: Only the routes that actually reach complete_setup carry the 8 rows. One call on this endpoint opens anything, and it sits on 5 of the 14 routes (setup in progress · consent required · replay · already done · first run). The nine that end earlier — the two rate limits, the two framework exits, Not authenticated, invalid token, validation, Idempotency-Key required, uncaught — never call it and gain no rows at all, so "every route" overstates the cost of keeping it by almost three to one.
confirmed.evidence: recomputed from docs/design/workflow-panel/_lab-ep.js: `forms.inside.calls` has exactly one key with `opens` (apps/api/services/setup.py::complete_setup, n = {raises 4, commits 3, savepoints 1}); 5 of the 14 `forms.paths` chains contain it; _lab-ep-panels.js:3448-3461 appends insideRows only where `insideCall(F, c.fn)` has opens
confirmed.fix: keep: "Only the routes that reach {callName} keep records {insideRows} rows longer: the success routes and the conflict routes that come back from it. The routes that end before the handler calls it are unchanged." If a count is wanted, it needs a new token, the number of paths whose chain holds the opening call. Size stays none.
confirmed.why: I parsed _lab-ep.js. `forms.inside.calls` has one key with `opens` (services/setup.py::complete_setup, n = raises 4, commits 3, savepoints 1). Only 5 of the 14 `forms.paths` chains contain it: setup in progress, consent required, replay, already done and first run. The two 429s, both framework exits, both 401s, validation, Idempotency-Key required and uncaught never reach it. insideRows is appended only where `ins.opens.length` (_lab-ep-panels.js:3448-3461). "Every route" overstates the cost of the option that competes with Claude's pick.

confirmed.claim: "The sentences stay. They show on the hover of every command that counts nothing."
confirmed.problem: One of the four sentences can never be shown, on this endpoint or any other. A cell is only asked for its why when it is hollow or hatched; a blank cell returns from the builder before any card is bound, and nothing anywhere asks slotState for the blank state. So "this kind of element has no such slot" is drawn nowhere — the card already warns that one sentence never shows here, which makes the operator read the remaining three as live when only two are.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/_lab-ep-panels.js:2788 (blank returns before tipBind), :2797 (why only for hollow/hatched), :2816 (the blank sentence), :3148 (the only blank cell, no card); no slotState call site passes the fourth argument (:2931-:2999, :3315)
confirmed.fix: ok: "The sentences stay. On this endpoint only the measured-zero sentence shows. The ones about a reading that did not run and a feed with no form need a reading switched off or a feed without forms. The one about a kind with no such slot is drawn nowhere today, because a blank cell carries no hover." The card's `what` needs the same correction, since it names only the did-not-run sentence as unseen. Size stays none.
confirmed.why: The core claim holds. cellNode returns at _lab-ep-panels.js:2788 for a blank cell before any tipBind. `why` is computed only for hollow or hatched cells (:2797). No slotState call passes the fourth argument (:2931-2999, :3315), and the only blank cell is padding (:3148). So "this kind of element has no such slot" is drawn nowhere. The finding's fix is wrong on one point: the no-form sentence does not show here either. _lab-ep.js has forms.state = 'present' with all eight arms on, and slotWhy returns that sentence only when armsOn(F) is null. On this endpoint only the measured-zero sentence shows.

confirmed.claim: "The roster leaves the design. Once built, every navigation in a branch reads as a call no idiom matches, still visible by its name."
confirmed.problem: useNavigate is one of six navigation rosters in the design. Dropping it leaves router.push/replace/navigate, the Next redirect calls, the static NextResponse/Response redirects, window.location.assign/replace/reload and the reused NAV_ELEMENTS / NAV_THROWS all classing normally — only the `const navigate = useNavigate(); navigate(...)` idiom falls through. The sentence prices the strike as losing every navigation.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/element-forms/plans/slice-11e-does.plan.json `plan.rosters`: NAV_BINDERS (useNavigate) beside NAV_ROUTER_BINDERS, NAV_ROUTER_METHODS, NAV_CALLS, NAV_STATIC, NAV_PLATFORM, plus reused NAV_ELEMENTS / NAV_THROWS (:8-9 of _a3_forms_fe.py)
confirmed.fix: no: "The useNavigate entry leaves the design. Once built, a navigation made through that hook, which is how react-router and TanStack Router apps such as gustify and gastify navigate from code, reads as a call no idiom matches, still visible by its name. router.push, the Next redirects, location.assign and the <Navigate> element keep classing as a move to another screen." The why needs the same correction. Size stays design.
confirmed.why: slice-11e-does.plan.json plan.rosters lists NAV_BINDERS {useNavigate} beside NAV_ROUTER_BINDERS, NAV_ROUTER_METHODS (push, replace, navigate), NAV_CALLS (redirect, permanentRedirect), NAV_STATIC, NAV_PLATFORM and the reused NAV_ELEMENTS and NAV_THROWS. Dropping the one entry loses only the `const navigate = useNavigate()` idiom. The roster comment cites react-router and TanStack Router for it, which are gustify's and gastify's routers, so on the two twins the loss is still large, but "every navigation" is false. The card's why ("Without it every navigation in a branch reads as an unknown call") repeats the overstatement.

confirmed.claim: "Once built, a toast call is classed as shown to the user, and the row says whether the name came from a library or from the project."
confirmed.problem: The design's own risk says the second half is unproven. No study app installs sonner, react-hot-toast or react-toastify, so the library side is cited from public API shape only; and for tier3's own toast the plan states outright that the expectation that its rows carry `from: fe:…#toast` through the tsconfig paths was not confirmed by any capture, because tier3 has no node_modules and is parsed with a borrowed typescript. The impact states the provenance row as a certainty.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/element-forms/plans/slice-11e-does.plan.json `plan.risks[5]`: "They are justified by public API shape only. tier3's 135-file `toast` is a project module. The expectation that its rows carry `from: fe:…#toast` … was not confirmed by any capture"
confirmed.fix: yes: "The design keeps toast. Once built, a toast call is classed as shown to the user. That the row also says whether the name came from a library or from the project is the design's expectation, not something captured. No study app installs one of the libraries, and tier3's own toast could not be captured because that app has no install, so the first dry run on tier3 is what proves it." Size stays design.
confirmed.why: plan.risks[5] says `surface` is cited to packages no study app installs and is justified by public API shape only. It also says the expectation that tier3's rows carry `from: fe:…#toast` through the tsconfig paths "was not confirmed by any capture: tier3 has no node_modules and is parsed with a borrowed typescript". plan.risks[6] adds that matching is by leaf with no binding disproof and "the `from` key is the only tell". The impact and the why both state the provenance row as certain. The card's `what` already admits no app installs a library, so the hidden part is the unproven `from` row.

confirmed.claim: "3 generator files change, the frontend battery gains a fixture and new cases, then come the dry runs on the four study apps, the doctor, and both app twins, whose centres regenerate. After it the ON THE CLIENT section gains the row …"
confirmed.problem: The three generator files and the battery are right, but three landing steps are left out, one of them the step that actually puts the row in the lab. The plan's 19 steps also carry: five new goldens plus the ARM map row and a re-rendered acceptance sheet; docs in the same commit (generators README, CLAUDE.md, the amendment's as-built block); and step 18, a SECOND commit — the lab carry — touching gen-endpoint-facts.py, _ep_joins.py, _lab-ep-panels.js and a new probe assert and mutant, browser-gated. Until that last commit the ON THE CLIENT section gains nothing.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/element-forms/plans/slice-11e-does.plan.json `plan.landing_order` steps 13 (goldens + render-acceptance), 14 (docs), 18 ("Lab carry, in its own commit closing leftovers piece 10 … COST: the probe is browser-gated, minutes, alone")
confirmed.fix: land: "I build the part, starting with the spec block in the amendment that records your rulings below. {p10files} generator files change, the frontend battery gains a fixture and new cases and the existing asserts the fixture moves are updated, the goldens and the acceptance sheet follow, then the dry runs on the four study apps, the doctor, the docs and both app twins, whose centres regenerate. A second commit then carries it into the lab, with a fresh all-arms feed, the facts script, the joins, the panel and a new probe assert, and only after that does the ON THE CLIENT section gain the row, on the {feReaders} endpoints whose client reads failures." Size stays generator.
confirmed.why: plan.landing_order confirms the omissions. Step 13 adds five goldens, the ARM map row and a re-rendered acceptance.html. Step 14 is docs in the same commit. Step 18 is "Lab carry, in its own commit": an all-arms gustify feed, gen-endpoint-facts.py --forms, _ep_joins.py:278, _lab-ep-panels.js:2835, a probe assert and a mutant, browser-gated. "After it the ON THE CLIENT section gains the row" reads as if the twins deliver the row, when the row exists only after that second, lab-sized commit. confirmed.claim: "first a lift out of one existing arm …, then a new module, a battery, the dry runs, the doctor and both twins. About four days, during which piece 10 waits."
confirmed.problem: The enumeration stops at the twins, which is step 12 of 15. Step 13 is the lab carry — the piece's second half, its own commit, about a day — and until it lands nothing about in-flight state appears in the lab, which is the reason for building it. The plan's own numbers add to roughly three and a half days through step 12 and roughly four and a half with the carry, so "about four days" is the generation half only.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/element-forms/plans/kinds-inflight.plan.json `plan.landing_order`: step 1 ~half a day · 2 ~2 h · 3 ~1 h · 4 ~1.5 days · 5 ~1 day · 8 ~1 h · 13 "THE LAB CARRY — the piece's second half, a second commit (~1 day)"
confirmed.fix: now: "I start it before piece 10. First comes a spec you approve again, with rulings this page does not ask (the slot U15 and the 12b order). Then come the lift out of one existing arm that must leave its output byte for byte the same, the new module, a battery, the dry runs, the doctor and both twins. Nothing shows in the lab until a second commit carries it there. By the plan's own step estimates that is about three and a half days to the twins and about one more for the lab, and piece 10 waits the whole time." The day figures come from plan.landing_order steps 1-5, 8 and 13. No token carries them, so gen-review should lift them or the total should be dropped. ui.s4note ("About four days of work") must agree. Size stays generator.
confirmed.why: kinds-inflight.plan.json plan.landing_order gives step 1 about half a day, step 2 about 2 h, step 3 about 1 h, step 4 about 1.5 days, step 5 about 1 day and step 8 about 1 h. That is roughly three and a half days through the twins (step 12). Step 13 is "THE LAB CARRY — the piece's second half, a second commit (~1 day)". The sentence stops at the twins and says "about four days", a typed figure that no token or fact carries. Finding 22 adds that step 1 is a spec needing fresh rulings; one final sentence covers both.

confirmed.claim: "The same build without the rows for values a helper hands to the handler. The design does not say how much that saves, so I would measure it first and tell you."
confirmed.problem: The design does say what the cut costs, even if not what it saves: the dependency-value detector is one of the first four pieces of the module, and the plan states that those first four alone are what reproduce the piece's five gustify after_rows — the very rows the operator was shown. Cutting it is not the same build minus some time; it is the build minus part of the worked example it was sold on.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/element-forms/plans/kinds-inflight.plan.json `plan.landing_order` step 4: "Build order inside: `_visit` and `_census` -> stations … -> D1 state -> D3 dependency-value -> … The first four alone reproduce the piece's five gustify after_rows"; step 1 lists "dependency-value rows in or out" as one of four rulings wanted before code
confirmed.fix: small: "The same build without the rows for values a helper hands to the handler. One of the rows this card shows under what piece 11 would say is such a row, the login context built by get_auth_context, so it would not appear, and neither would the database session's row. The design does not say how much time that saves, so I would measure it first and tell you." Size stays generator.
confirmed.why: The plan's D3 detector says dependency-value rows are "in the piece's after_rows and D-013's three known instances". The worked schema row is `kind: dependency-value, name: ctx, dependency: …get_auth_context`. The card's own FACTS.p11.after[1], "login context · built by get_auth_context (auth/context.py:90) · read by the handler · gone with the answer", is exactly such a row. plan.lab_carry also relies on these rows for the session teardown row and for the join that gives a gate its value. So `small` removes one of the rows the card shows as what piece 11 would say, which the sentence hides.

confirmed.id: norm line · ok (norm_impacts.ok, applies to all 36 lines)
confirmed.claim: "The line stays as it is. It keeps showing on the hover of that stage, in that topic." — size `none`.

The lab reads the norm registry in exactly three places, and all three read `STAGE_EXPECT.data` — the DATA topic — inside `renderDataStageBlocks`, which is gated to `part === "data"`. The 30 lines under Schemas, Functions, Tests, Widening and Security are drawn NOWHERE today. So on 30 of the lines he is ruling one by one, "ok" keeps a line no hover shows and "reword" rewrites a line nobody reads — the operator is spending his most expensive attention (the page's own order: "what I wrote comes first, because no check can catch a wrong sentence") on sentences with no surface.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/_lab-ep-panels.js:1237 declares the registry with 6 topics × 6 stages; its ONLY readers are :1314, :1319 and :1373, each `(STAGE_EXPECT.data || {})[…]`; :3354 gates the stage machinery with `part === "data"`; :3587/:3600 register `stageblocks` as the DATA panel's default variant. docs/design/workflow-panel/probe-eplab.mjs:3307-3308 states it out loud: "the six lines live in one registry the next topics add beside".
confirmed.fix: Same final sentence as finding 0. ok: "The line stays as it is. Only the Data topic's lines are drawn today: on the stage header's hover, on the 'also at' card, and as the text of a stage with no table. The lines of the other topics are written but drawn nowhere yet, so ruling them settles the words before their surface exists." Size stays none.
confirmed.why: This is the same defect as finding 0, with the same evidence. STAGE_EXPECT is read only at :1314, :1319 and :1373, all `.data`, inside the Data part's stage-blocks machinery, and probe :3307-3308 says "the six lines live in one registry the next topics add beside". confirmed.id: norm line · strike (norm_impacts.strike, applies to all 36 lines)
confirmed.claim: "I remove the line. That stage then shows no expectation for that topic, and says so, never a blank." — size `words`.
confirmed.problem: Two wrongs in one sentence. (a) On a DATA line the lab prints exactly a blank: a stage with no table appends `esc(STAGE_EXPECT.data[key])`, and `esc` returns "" for a missing value — an empty `.sbnone` div, not a sentence, until the lab's code gains a fallback. (b) The probe pins the registry's shape twice: every topic's keys must equal 'EDGE,GATE,INPUT,HANDLER,EFFECTS,ANSWER', and the data topic's keys the same six. Any strike turns both red. That is lab code plus a probe rewrite, not "words only" — and the operator has 36 chances to pick it.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/_lab-ep-panels.js:1373 (`body.append(E("div", { class: "sbnone" }, esc((STAGE_EXPECT.data || {})[s.key])))`) and :21 (`esc(s){ return String(s == null ? "" : s)…}`); docs/design/workflow-panel/probe-eplab.mjs:3016 + :3019 (six keys per topic) and :3307-3308 (the data topic's six keys).
confirmed.fix: Same final sentence as finding 1. strike: "I remove the line. Where the lab draws it, which today is the Data topic only, a missing line would show as an empty space, so I add a fallback that says the stage has no expectation for that topic. The probe asserts that pin a line for every stage of every topic are rewritten with it." Size: lab.
confirmed.why: This is the same defect as finding 1. :1373 with esc() at :21 draws an empty `.sbnone` div for a missing Data line. Probe :3016 and :3019 pin six keys per topic, :3308 pins the Data six, and :3304 also fails for four of the Data lines. A fallback in lab code plus a probe rewrite is `lab` by the page's vocabulary, not `words`.

confirmed.claim: size `none` — "The place stays on the whole-app card, and your older ruling on the risk card stands."
confirmed.problem: The decision's own WHAT promises a change under every option: "Whatever you rule, I correct the count so it reads of 80 endpoints, since the startup is not one." That count is generated, and it is not a label: the same ranking that gives `of: 81` gives `rank: 11`, `behind_max: 135` and `behind_max_of: "BOOT lifespan"`. Taking the startup out moves the place to 10th and makes the heaviest GET /recipes at 48 — a facts change plus the probe line that reads `behind_max_of` back off the card. Tagging this option `none` ("a choice that leaves the lab and the map exactly as they are") tells the operator the pick is free when it is the only option whose cost is hidden in the WHAT instead of the impact.
confirmed.evidence: docs/design/workflow-panel/gen-endpoint-facts.py:542 (`_rank`), :552-554 (`"of": n_endpoints`, `behind_max`, `behind_max_of`, `heaviest`); the live feed `_lab-ep.js` context.risk = {of: 81, rank: 11, behind_max: 135, behind_max_of: "BOOT lifespan"}; probe-eplab.mjs:2798 asserts the card contains `' of ' + C7.R.of` and `C7.R.behind_max_of`.
confirmed.fix: everything: "The place stays on the whole-app card, and your older ruling on the risk card stands. The count correction still happens, and it is a facts change: the card then reads {placeEp} of {appEndpoints}, and the biggest it names is an endpoint instead of {placeTop}." refuted.id: p11-name · keep / alive / rename (and p11 · drop)
